claim: Minimal disruption of the native transcriptome was validated in three GSH sites in vitro using hESCs and their differentiated progeny.

claim: A total of 12,766 sites passed the computational filters for safe genomic locations.

evidence: Supported by computational analysis results shown in Figure 1

claim: The 12,766 sites that passed filters range from 1 b to approximately 30 Mb.
source: A total of 12,766 sites, ranging from 1 b to approximately 30 Mb, passed the filters used (Figure 1A–B; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by computational analysis results

claim: 399 1 Mb active regions overlapped with a ubiquitously expressed gene.
source: This analysis yielded 399 1 Mb active regions that overlapped with a ubiquitously expressed gene (Figure 1A–B; Supplementary file 1).

claim: 49 safe sites were found within the active regions.
source: By overlapping the two datasets, we found 49 safe sites within the active regions.
evidence: Supported by computational analysis results

claim: BLAT was used to remove candidate sites that had highly similar sequence matches at other genomic loci.

evidence: Supported by description of computational methods

claim: Successful heterozygous targeting of the donor construct was confirmed at three candidate GSH sites on chromosomes 1, 18, and 19.
source: Successful heterozygous targeting of the donor construct was confirmed at three candidate GSH sites on chromosomes 1, 18, and 19.
evidence: Supported by junction-PCR and digital-PCR data

claim: The three GSH sites were successfully targeted in H9 hESC for validation in an independent cell line.
source: These three GSH sites were subsequently also targeted in H9 hESC for validation in an independent cell line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: No evidence of off-target activity was observed following PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing of the top five predicted off-target sites for each of the targeted clones.
source: No evidence of off-target activity was observed following PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing of the top five predicted off-target sites for each of the targeted clones (Figure 2—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: Supported by Sanger sequencing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 2–4

claim: The successfully targeted safe harbours were named Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19.
source: We named the successfully targeted safe harbours after real world harbours, designating them Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19.
evidence: Explicit naming statement in the manuscript

claim: The mean log2 fold-change values of the three nearest genes in the three H1 GSH clones ranged from –0.067 to 0.065 when compared to un-targeted H1 hESCs.
source: When compared to un-targeted H1 hESCs, the mean log2 fold-change (log2-FC) values of the three nearest genes in the three H1 GSH clones as well as an independent un-targeted H1 sample ranged from –0.067 to 0.065 (Figure 2C, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C

claim: The results from the same comparison with H9 lines ranged from log2-FC of –0.14 to 0.04.
source: The results from same comparison with our established H9 lines ranged from log2-FC of –0.14 to 0.04 (Figure 2–figure supplement 5, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2–figure supplement 5

claim: Only three one sample Student's t-tests on the log2-FC results showed p-values of less than 0.05.
source: Only three one sample Student's t-tests on the log2-FC results showed p-values of less than 0.05, including the H1 vs. H1 comparison of MAGI3 (Figure 2C, Figure 2–figure supplement 5, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis of qPCR data

claim: Pairwise comparisons of GSH targeted clones to un-targeted H1 hESCs yielded 96, 111, and 119 differentially expressed genes out of 29,696 observed genes for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19 respectively.
source: Pairwise comparisons of our GSH targeted clones to un-targeted H1 hESCs yielded very low numbers of differentially expressed (DE) genes; 96, 111, and 119 out of 29,696 observed genes respectively for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19 and 260 genes for independent H1 un-targeted samples (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: CASP9 was the gene with lowest false discovery rate in all three GSH lines.
source: Notably CASP9, the suicide gene included in our targeting construct, was the gene with lowest false discovery rate (FDR) in all three GSH lines (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: A high proportion of the DE genes found in GSH targeted lines were shared with the DE genes found from pair-wise comparisons of the independent set of wild-type H1 cells to the un-targeted H1 hESCs.
source: A high proportion of the DE genes found in our GSH targeted lines were shared with the DE genes found from pair-wise comparisons of the independent set of wild-type H1 cells to the un-targeted H1 hESCs (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E

claim: RNAseq analysis on the H9 GSH targeted lines yielded 60, 51, and 91 differentially expressed genes out of 35,070 observed genes for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19 respectively.
source: Same RNAseq analysis on the H9 GSH targeted lines also yielded a low number of DE genes; 60, 51, and 91 out of 35,070 observed genes respectively for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19 (Figure 2–figure supplement 5 and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2–figure supplement 5

claim: The closest DE gene found from the analysis in both H1 and H9 cells lies >3 Mb away for Pansio-1, >5 Mb for Olônne-18 and approximately 1 Mb for Keppel-19.
source: The closest DE gene found from our analysis in both H1 and H9 cells lies >3 Mb away for Pansio-1, >5 Mb for Olônne-18 and approximately 1 Mb for Keppel-19 (Supplementary files 5 and 6).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis

claim: None of the DE genes shared across the H1 and H9 cells are located on the same chromosome as the respective GSH loci that were targeted, except CASP9 and Pansio-1 on chromosome 1.
source: None of the DE genes shared across the H1 and H9 cells are located on the same chromosome as the respective GSH loci that were targeted (Supplementary file 5), except CASP9, part of our targeting construct, and Pansio-1 on chromosome 1.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis

claim: Functional enrichment analysis of the DE genes revealed 2, 15, and 25 terms in H1 cells for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19, respectively.
source: Functional enrichment analysis of the DE genes revealed relatively few terms; 2, 15, and 25 in H1 cells and 6, 5, and 18 in H9 for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19, respectively (Supplementary files 5 and 6).
evidence: Supported by functional enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data

claim: Functional enrichment analysis of the DE genes revealed 6, 5, and 18 terms in H9 cells for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19, respectively.
source: Functional enrichment analysis of the DE genes revealed relatively few terms; 2, 15, and 25 in H1 cells and 6, 5, and 18 in H9 for Pansio-1, Olônne-18, and Keppel-19, respectively (Supplementary files 5 and 6).
evidence: Supported by functional enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data

claim: No karyotypic abnormalities were observed in the established H1 and H9 lines.
source: As a further safety check, we also conducted karyotyping of the established H1 and H9 lines and observed no abnormalities (Figure 2–figure supplement 6).
evidence: Supported by karyotyping data shown in Figure 2–figure supplement 6

claim: All three GSH lines were able to give rise to tissues from endoderm, ectoderm, and mesoderm lineages in teratomas.
source: All three lines were able to give rise to tissues from endoderm, ectoderm, and mesoderm lineages (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: Supported by teratoma data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7

claim: Clover targeted GSH lines maintained >98% Clover-positive cells over 15 passages.
source: We maintained the Clover targeted GSH lines in hESC state over 15 passages and consistently observed >98% Clover-positive cells (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).

claim: Clover expression remained consistent in neuronal, liver, and cardiac cells differentiated from Clover-integrated hESC lines.

claim: Clover-transgene expression was observed in marker-positive pancreatic β-cells differentiated from Pansio-1 targeted H9 line.

claim: Quantification of high-content imaging indicated high correlation of the lineage markers and the Clover transgene signal, ranging from 75% to 99%.

claim: Twenty-four hour incubation with 1 µg/ml doxycycline was sufficient to drive expression of the GFP transgene on average in 73% of cells.
